title: Monthly meter volume figures passed by hand to schedulers
label_mechanical: Meter data requests and corrections: report meter / volume / data

narrative.what_happens: Within the gas logistics mailbox, someone circulates volume figures for named meters — typically for a given month — to the colleagues who need them. Most of these messages are one-way notifications: a meter number and its volumes are stated and sent on, with no request attached. A smaller number are confirmations back that the figures for the month are agreed, and in one case a breakdown of a meter's volumes by counterparty is forwarded with a note that the recipient may or may not need it. The exchange ends when the recipient has the number; nothing in the evidence shows a downstream system being updated as a result.
narrative.where_it_stalls: There is no visible stall in these messages: none carry waiting, rework or deadline signals, and there are no escalation or correction roles. What the evidence does show is that the figures move as prose in mail rather than out of a system — one message carries a manual-transfer signal and hedges on whether the recipient even needs the data ("not sure if you need this"), so the sender is guessing at the distribution rather than working from a defined recipient list.
narrative.why_it_recurs: Meter volumes are reported per month, so the same figures have to be restated each accounting period, and the recipients are chosen ad hoc each time rather than by a standing list.
narrative.automation_opportunity: A scheduled extract that pulls the month's volumes for each meter from the volume-accounting source and mails each scheduler only their own meters would remove the need for anyone to retype or judge who needs the figures. Given how few messages this cluster holds, a standing recipient list per meter would capture most of the benefit on its own.

steps: 11.00 task instances / 5 months of coverage = 2.200 instances per month
minutes per instance = 9 handle + (1.18 touches - 1) x 4 + 0.00 rework rate x 12 + 0.00 waiting rate x 3 = 9.73 min
